hypotheses.claim: ClayCode needs two independent fail-closed closures at the effect boundary: runtime bearer-authority closure and evidence/admission closure. Passing one never implies the other.
hypotheses.prediction: A bearer-valid runtime can still have an inadmissible gate result when execution provenance, exact subject/material digests or scope are missing; conversely a perfectly attested build cannot authorize an effect without a live valid capability handle.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single mechanism can safely and unambiguously provide both runtime effect authority and historical execution-evidence admission without creating a bearer/provenance confusion or replay path.

hypotheses.claim: Workflow presence and optimistic commit naming are not sufficient evidence that a ClayCode gate executed successfully.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one current workflow-labelled gate will lack its declared result receipt or a verifiable executed-run binding on the default branch.
hypotheses.result: Observed for both WP03 typed-IR workflow and runtime capability workflow: workflow-definition commits exist while expected committed receipt files were absent at inspection time.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current branch contains a verified successful run plus exact declared receipt for each inspected gate, bound to the inspected source/test versions.

hypotheses.claim: A GateExecutionAttestation should bind immutable subject digests to test/material digests, execution identity, conclusion, evidence scope and admission policy; release state should advance only after verification of that bundle.
hypotheses.prediction: Mutation of head/source/test/workflow digest, run state, receipt presence, test result, negative-control result or execution scope will fail closed while a fully matched bundle admits.
hypotheses.falsifier: A required field can be removed or mutated without producing a plausible stale/forged/mis-scoped admission case, showing that the field is unnecessary or wrongly placed.

hypotheses.claim: For in-process ClayCode/Frank execution, opaque runtime-instance-bound capability handles are preferable to serializable bearer records; cross-process FFI should use a broker/table/OS-handle representation rather than treating serialized Clay records as authority.
hypotheses.prediction: Copying or reconstructing a capability-shaped value fails, while a broker-owned live handle/index can be passed according to adapter rules.
hypotheses.falsifier: A serializable Clay capability record can be made equally safe under the required replay/restart/FFI threat model without confusing description, provenance and authority.

hypotheses.claim: Hosted GitHub Ubuntu CI and Andreas' Ubuntu developer system must remain distinct evidence scopes even when they execute byte-identical runtime/test inputs.
hypotheses.prediction: A hosted-CI receipt can support regression confidence but cannot alone satisfy target-host acceptance; the target receipt may reference the same subject/material digests while carrying a different execution-scope identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: The project acceptance contract is explicitly changed so hosted GitHub Ubuntu is an accepted substitute for the Andreas target host.

hypotheses.claim: Attestation/provenance is never execution authority. A verified GateExecutionAttestation may admit evidence but must not be accepted by the effect broker as a CapabilityHandle.
hypotheses.prediction: Supplying a valid attestation object where a runtime capability is required always fails type/identity validation.
hypotheses.falsifier: A project-owner-approved effect model intentionally defines a signed attestation as a bearer capability and supplies revocation/delegation/liveness semantics equivalent to the current runtime authority model.

counterhypotheses.claim: Git commit history around a workflow is enough; no explicit gate attestation/receipt binding is needed.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Attempt to prove from current default-branch state that the runtime capability tests actually executed successfully against the exact current runtime and validation files.
counterhypotheses.result: The workflow-definition commit and expected receipt path were observable, but the expected receipt was absent; commit title alone therefore did not establish executed success.

counterhypotheses.claim: Plain committed JSON receipts with exact hashes and run identity are sufficient for BASE; cryptographic builder attestation would add complexity without useful admission discrimination.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Compare threat models: accidental stale/mis-scoped admission versus malicious repository writer/builder forgery. Plain receipts may solve the former while signed builder provenance targets the latter.

counterhypotheses.claim: Capability object identity checks are too process-local for the eventual ClayCode runtime ABI/FFI and should be replaced immediately by portable MAC-bearing serialized tokens.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Implement the actual first Ubuntu adapter boundary and test whether capability authority ever needs to cross a process/serialization boundary. If not, process-local opacity is simpler and safer for BASE.

counterhypotheses.claim: The V4/V6/V7 grammar drift is harmless because semantic-source authority remains G9/Dialect and downstream receipts bind current grammar hashes anyway.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Inspect actual frontend/typed-IR receipts after they exist and test cross-version semantic-hash equivalence.

promotion.reason: Current evidence supports a concrete admission constraint and implementation candidate but target-host production receipts are still missing.
